title: Georgekutty Comes Home. Drishyam 3 Lands on Prime Video Today — and the Diaspora Doesn't Have to Hunt for a Theatre Anymore.
excerpt: Mohanlal's masterclass in the slow, deliberate cover-up streams worldwide from June 18 in five languages. After ₹236 crore at the box office, the most patient man in Indian cinema is back to outthink everyone in your living room.
body:
There is a particular kind of dread Mohanlal has perfected over three films, and it has nothing to do with jump scares. It is the dread of a man who knows something you don't, who has already played the next four moves while everyone around him is still reacting to the first. Watch his eyes in any frame of the Drishyam trilogy and you see it — the calculation running quietly behind a face that gives away nothing. Georgekutty doesn't panic. Georgekutty plans. And from June 18, the whole world gets to watch him do it again, from the couch.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=07h9Y1XKBWI

Drishyam 3 began streaming on Amazon Prime Video today, four weeks after a theatrical run that turned into the highest-grossing Malayalam film of the year, crossing ₹236 crore worldwide. For the diaspora — the Mallayalis in New Jersey and the suspense junkies in Toronto who couldn't find a screen near them — this is the moment the wait pays off. No more scanning for a lone late-night show at a suburban multiplex. It's there, in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Hindi, the moment you open the app.

"For the diaspora — the Mallayalis in New Jersey and the suspense junkies in Toronto who couldn't find a screen near them — this is the moment the wait pays off."
"Mohanlal proves Georgekutty is still one step ahead of everyone." — Mathrubhumi review, May 2026

Director Jeethu Joseph, the architect of this whole gorgeous house of cards, returns to wrap up the story he started back in 2013 — though, this being Drishyam, "wrap up" comes with an asterisk. The new chapter picks up years after the events of Drishyam 2, with Georgekutty living the uneasy life of a man who has gotten away with it. He's wealthy now. Successful. And quietly terrified that the single secret he has buried under layers of misdirection might claw its way to the surface. When Varun's grieving parents join forces with the law to lay an elaborate trap for his daughter Anju — a fake marriage proposal engineered to frame her — Georgekutty is pulled back into the only game he has ever truly mastered.

The casting reads like a Drishyam family reunion: Meena returns as Rani, the wife who has lived inside this lie almost as long as her husband; Asha Sarath is back to bring the cold, methodical fury of a mother who has never stopped wanting answers; Ansiba Hassan and Esther Anil reprise the daughters who are, in their own way, the entire reason the franchise has any heart at all. Add Siddique, Murali Gopy and Kalabhavan Shajon, and you have an ensemble that knows exactly how to hold tension across a two-and-a-half hour runtime without ever letting it snap.

What makes the Drishyam films work — and what makes them travel so well across borders — is that they're not really thrillers about crime. They're thrillers about a father, and how far an ordinary man will go to protect the people he loves. That's a story that lands the same in Kochi and in Calgary. It's why a Malayalam film with no item numbers and no glossy action set-pieces became a pan-Indian phenomenon that Bollywood remade, that Hindi audiences embraced, that streaming platforms fought a public legal war over. Earlier this year, Prime Video issued a pointed warning staking its sole digital rights to the film — a reminder of just how valuable Georgekutty has become as intellectual property.

Critics, for their part, have been admiring if a touch divided. The Hollywood Reporter India called it "Mohanlal in all his elements in this mostly satisfying conclusion," while The Quint noted that Joseph "wraps up the final chapter, but not the suspense" — which, frankly, is the most Drishyam thing imaginable. A clean ending was never the point. The point is the journey of watching a man manipulate a crime scene, manage a narrative, and stay three steps ahead of everyone in the room, including, sometimes, the audience.

If you've never entered this world, today is the rare chance to start a trilogy knowing all three films are a click away. And if you've been with Georgekutty since the beginning, you already know the drill: dim the lights, put your phone away, and trust nothing you see. The man who taught a generation that the perfect alibi is built from the smallest, most boring details is back. Watch closely. He's counting on you not to.

Drishyam 3 is streaming now on Amazon Prime Video in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Hindi — available worldwide for diaspora viewers in the US, UK, Canada and beyond.
